target_customer: Front-end engineers and design teams building React component libraries
problem: Designers and engineers work in separate tools, so design-system components drift from production code.
business_model: Design tool subscription (a pricing aggregator lists $29 per month; unverified)

founders.name: Emil Sjölander
education: Design student, Sweden (school not stated on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Front-end infrastructure engineer; creator and core contributor to Yoga, Litho, React Native and Flipper per the YC page. Later an engineering manager at Figma.

founders.name: Karl Petersson
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given.

competitors.name: Framer X
competitors.what: Design tool that works with React components

competitors.name: Sketch2React
competitors.what: Design with real React code inside Sketch, with export

competitors.name: React Proto
competitors.what: Prototyping and design tool for React applications

competitors.name: Indigo.Design (Infragistics)
competitors.what: Design-to-code workflow across Sketch and Visual Studio Code

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual editor that outputs code engineers would trust needs a rendering engine, component model and code import tooling, which is hard for a team of six.

defensibility.rationale: Several design-to-code tools already existed in 2018 and Figma and Adobe XD were well funded, so a small team had little structural advantage besides the founder's open source reputation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Figma acquired Visly (undated in sources found) and the visly.app domain now redirects to figma.com.

market_need_then: Component-driven front-end development and shared design systems were spreading in 2018, per the company's own pitch; independent demand evidence was not found.

branding.domain_note: Used visly.app, not a .com; the domain now redirects to figma.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched with an engineer-first voice about earning trust from the engineering community (company description).

brand_strength.rationale: Little press or community coverage was found; the name is easily mixed up with Visily (a different wireframing company) in search results.

outcome_analysis: Visly pursued a design tool aimed at engineers and was acquired by Figma, with a founder later working as an engineering manager at Figma. No funding, price or date of the deal was found, so whether it was an acquihire or a product purchase is unknown. The product category was crowded and dominated by well-funded design tool companies, and the founders' standing in the React open source community was their distinctive asset.
notes: The company site visly.app redirects to figma.com (301). The acquisition date, price and terms were not found; the only direct source is an undated Figma forum post and the redirect. A different company named Visily (visily.ai) appears in search results and its funding must not be attributed to Visly. Competitor entries come from search result titles and snippets dated 2018; the pages were not individually opened.
